decisions.rejected: making all three async void, which would drop the record on exactly the crash the flush exists for

decisions.decision: DevWinUI stays at 10.8.0
decisions.why: DevWinUI 11.1.0 references WinRT.Runtime 2.3.1.0 while this platform's projection supplies 2.2.0.0, so the build fails with CS1705 and a masked WMC9999; resolving it needs a Windows SDK projection change no approved proposal authorises
decisions.rejected: pinning Microsoft.Windows.CsWinRT across every project, which is outside the register

decisions.decision: SUPERSEDES the decision above: DevWinUI moves to 11.1.0, and the WinRT.Runtime projection is pinned through WindowsSdkPackageVersion 10.0.28000.87 in Directory.Build.props
decisions.why: the original diagnosis treated the projection as a machine-level fact. It is a per-project package the .NET SDK picks from the target platform version, and WindowsSdkPackageVersion is the property Microsoft documents for overriding it. Microsoft.Windows.SDK.NET.Ref 10.0.28000.87 is the first release that ships WinRT.Runtime 2.3.1.0; every release up to 10.0.26100.57 ships 2.2.0.0. With the pin the CS1705 is gone, the solution builds at 0 warnings and 0 errors, the suite is 2,915 passed / 66 skipped / 0 failed, and the running application reaches sign-in, the shell, Settings, Work Center Setup and the WindowedContentDialog form. No approved proposal had to change: DEP-007 always targeted 11.1.0
decisions.rejected: waiting for a platform release, which was the original condition and was wrong about what the block was; and pinning Microsoft.Windows.CsWinRT by PackageReference, which the documentation does not recommend for this

decisions.decision: Six collection expressions in the test project carry an explicit array cast
decisions.why: the projection pin brings the CsWinRT1032 authoring analyzer, which refuses a collection expression whose target is a non-mutable interface type. The cast names the concrete type the compiler was already synthesizing, so behaviour is unchanged and the warning count stayed at 0
decisions.rejected: suppressing CsWinRT1032, which would hide the same shape wherever it appears next

decisions.decision: The reviewed queue-script route is a separate contract rather than a member of the data seam
decisions.why: The seam rule stays true: no member of it can run statement text, and the reader takes a name from the reviewed set so a caller cannot widen it
decisions.rejected: Keeping ExecuteSqlQueryAsync on the seam, or converting the queue scripts to stored procedures, which is database authoring this feature does not do

decisions.decision: The test project statement route stayed as internal members of the seam implementation
decisions.why: About fifty database-gated fixture call sites seed and verify rows with raw statements; moving them would duplicate connection resolution into the test project. InternalsVisibleTo keeps them unreachable from application code and InlineSqlAuditTests confines them
decisions.rejected: Deleting them from the class and rewriting thirteen integration suites, or giving the tests a private connection factory

decisions.decision: The Infor Visual executor takes the module instead of keeping two types
decisions.why: One owner of the read path; the module chooses only the script folder, so the setup tool keeps its own queue scripts and its own log tag
decisions.rejected: Resolving both module folders from one path, which would let a caller reach another module scripts

decisions.decision: The mock-service generated context carries the ignore-null and string-enum settings as context options

decisions.rejected: One context per store

decisions.decision: The dynamic mirror payload stays on the reflection writer

decisions.decision: IGenericRequestSubmitter lives in the generic-request library and is implemented by GenericRequestSubmitter in Waitlist.View

approach: Eight ordered phases from section 14, each with a prerequisite gate and measured completion evidence, carried as 30 waves where a wave is one proposal or two text-only proposals sharing a review. Contract versions come from central package management first, then ascending runtime blast radius, then framework-native replacements, then architecture, then performance and strings, then the AI and design records.

concerns.note: W10 and W11 connectivity gates cannot run against the plant host in this environment; they are proven against the local instance and recorded as environment-gated, which principle VI allows

MOD-006 remedy departs from the source document: the dialog body is composed in code rather than moved to Module_, because MTM_Waitlist.Mock.Service also calls MessageDialogHost. Confirm against MessageDialogAdoptionTests before implementing W23

plan.md Phase 5 completion evidence reads "the seam executes stored procedures only and its raw-SQL allowlist is empty of service sites", but MTM_Waitlist.Core/Services/WipFloorInventoryService.cs is a reviewed and justified entry in the InlineSqlAuditTests allowlist that runs the checked-in MTM WIP queue scripts as command text. No approved proposal covers it and turning those scripts into stored procedures is database authoring, which the plan rules out, so W18 (T068 to T072) keeps one script-text route behind a narrowed seam, records the reason at the route and in the phase report, and the Phase 5 gate reads "the raw-SQL allowlist describes exactly the code that exists" instead of "empty of service sites".
